issues.description: The problem statement and UML require addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int plus a String reason) but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This parameter mismatch means students or automated tests expecting the two-parameter signature will be confused or fail to compile against the solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's method signature match the specification: change the method in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update its body to add the new guest students (and optionally record or log the reason). Alternatively, if the reason parameter is not needed, update the problem statement and UML to remove the String parameter so all artifacts agree.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int for new guest students plus a String reason), but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only the integer parameter. This mismatch in the method signature (missing the String reason parameter) creates a mapping confusion: students following the task/UML will implement or look for a two-parameter method while the reference solution exposes a one-parameter variant.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation match the problem/UML: change the solution (and template stub) to implement addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and handle or record the reason (even if only logged or ignored) so the method signature aligns with the exercise specification. Alternatively, if the reason parameter is intentionally unnecessary, update the problem statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) to avoid confusion.
